er_v06_c17_b101_01: A woman comes to the window in a gray coat, a care-office registration badge on her chest.
er_v06_c17_b101_02: Hello. East of the ration station, third shop window. This is it, right?
er_v06_c17_b101_03: Eleanor drew me a map. More detail than the shift rota back at our farm.
er_v06_c17_b101_05: She says you sell things, and you tell the faults first.
er_v06_c17_b101_06: I came for some daily goods. And to check that for myself.
er_v06_c17_b101_07: Left shelf. Top two bottles. Lids don't screw on tight.
er_v06_c17_b101_08: She goes to the left shelf, twists each of the two bottles in turn, puts them back, and takes the ones from the back row.
er_v06_c17_b101_09: They really don't. You didn't lie to her.
er_v06_c17_b101_10: Some nutrient fruit too. She drew a fruit on that map in the room.
er_v06_c17_b101_11: She picks up a nutrient fruit, presses the skin with her thumb, and turns it half around under the lamp.
er_v06_c17_b101_12: Ration station batches. Skin's dark. Hollow inside.
er_v06_c17_b101_13: Anyone can look up the data now. The kind you can actually grow — nobody's handed out seedlings yet.
er_v06_c17_b101_14: You're not going to do anything about it?
er_v06_c17_b101_15: The review isn't closed. I have to stay at the registered address. The guard calls my name twice a day.
er_v06_c17_b101_16: This morning a worker had the guard pass on a message. Asking if the next shift rotation is still on.
er_v06_c17_b101_17: I can't answer. The research belongs to everyone now. My hands are empty.
er_v06_c17_b101_18: Don't tell her that. She'll think it's her fault I lost my work.
er_v06_c17_b101_19: She sets the things on the counter, digs a few credits out of her coat pocket, and lays them out one by one.
er_v06_c17_b101_20: Did she tell you how she saved up those eight hundred credits?
er_v06_c17_b101_21: Selling salvage. One deal at a time.
er_v06_c17_b101_22: She used to barely look at price tags. She didn't tell me much about this.
er_v06_c17_b101_24: Don't charge me less just because I'm wearing this coat.
er_v06_c17_b101_25: She's been sleeping deep these days. Last night she talked in her sleep. Haggling with someone.
er_v06_c17_b101_26: If she wants to come, she'll come herself. I'm just here to buy things.
er_v06_c17_b101_27: She slips the nutrient fruits into her coat pocket, nods to the shopkeeper, and leaves.
er_v06_c18_b101_01: The next afternoon, two people come to the window, one behind the other. The first carries half a sack of secondhand goods.
er_v06_c18_b101_02: We agreed I'd be the one to bring her! Then she starts running over here by herself every day — what does that make me?
er_v06_c18_b101_03: It makes you the guide. I knew the way already.
er_v06_c18_b101_05: Just tell me—hasn't she been looking better lately? Face is a little rounder.
er_v06_c18_b101_06: Whose face is round. Cut it out.
er_v06_c18_b101_07: Lydia lifts her wrist and gives it a shake. The old bracelet glints under the light.
er_v06_c18_b101_08: I wear the bracelet every day. When my family asks, I say I found it myself.
er_v06_c18_b101_09: Oh, enough about the bracelet. I'm here to see her today.
er_v06_c18_b101_10: My family's been going through my accounts lately. I have to be back before dinner. I got her here.
er_v06_c18_b101_11: Next time I'll come on my own. I've got things to buy too. That's settled, then.
er_v06_c18_b101_13: One bracelet's worth of friendship. I'm off!
er_v06_c18_b101_14: Eleanor sets the sack on the counter. Metal parts clink inside; she takes her time untying it.
er_v06_c18_b101_15: She talks a lot. Don't take it all seriously.
er_v06_c18_b101_16: The room's registered now. Mother sleeps in the bed at the back.
er_v06_c18_b101_17: She came here yesterday. After she got back, she didn't say a word to me.
er_v06_c18_b101_18: She bought household goods, and something to eat.
er_v06_c18_b101_20: That's all. Paid the marked price.
er_v06_c18_b101_22: She opens the sack and tips out an old box, its lid split along a seam. And a roll of coiled wire.
er_v06_c18_b101_23: The crack's in the lid. The bottom's fine. I measured the wire myself. Nothing broken.
er_v06_c18_b101_25: Box goes as secondhand. Wire counts as a full roll.
er_v06_c18_b101_26: About what I figured. A little less and I'd still take it.
er_v06_c19_b101_01: The sky darkens and the streetlights come on one by one. She sits on the crate outside the window, tapping the ground with her toes.
er_v06_c19_b101_03: I know. I'm not buying anything.
er_v06_c19_b101_04: Mother's home. The guards just finished roll call. She'll cook her own nutrient fruit.
er_v06_c19_b101_05: She pulled the pendant out by its cord, gripped it in her palm, then tucked it back.
er_v06_c19_b101_06: Hey. I'm telling you something. Don't cut in.
er_v06_c19_b101_07: When I first came down here, I thought every pawnshop in the lower district was the same.
er_v06_c19_b101_08: That other place kept haggling me down and docking the purity. When they shorted me a few credits, I didn't come to you to make it up.
er_v06_c19_b101_09: But I keep coming here. You're not cheap either.
er_v06_c19_b101_10: What you did for my mother — I haven't forgotten.
er_v06_c19_b101_11: Don't think I'm paying off a debt.
er_v06_c19_b101_13: That's it. Do what you want.
er_v06_c19_b102_01: The shopkeeper reaches through the window. She lifts her hand from her knee and lets him take it.
er_v06_c19_b102_03: You answered so fast. Those words took me three days.
er_v06_c19_b102_04: I've thought about it longer than you.
er_v06_c19_b102_05: Hah. Then why didn't you say it first?
er_v06_c19_b102_06: You said not to make decisions for you.
er_v06_c19_b102_08: She didn't pull her hand back. She gripped his fingers instead, a little too hard.
er_v06_c19_b102_09: Let's get this straight. I still scavenge. I still sell. You misprice, I'll still call you out.
er_v06_c19_b102_10: I'm coming tomorrow. Even if I don't buy anything.
er_v06_c19_b102_11: My mother — I'll tell her myself. Don't you go.
er_v06_c19_b102_13: She stands, lets go of his hand, and steps back to leave room for the window shutter.
er_v06_c19_b103_01: I think of you as a friend. And I will going forward.
er_v06_c19_b103_02: ...Got it. You said it clear. Saves me guessing.
er_v06_c19_b103_03: I'll come tomorrow to sell. By the price tag — don't give up a single coin.
er_v06_c19_b103_04: She stands, pushes the crate back beside the window, and leaves.
er_v06_c18_b101_27: She puts the coins in her purse, ties it twice, and stays at the window.
